def test_is_nested():
    # Basic cases from the specification
    assert is_nested('[[]]') == True          # single nesting
    assert is_nested('[]]]]]]][[[[[]') == False
    assert is_nested('[][]') == False         # no nesting, just sequential
    assert is_nested('[]') == False           # single pair, no nesting
    assert is_nested('[[][]]') == True        # nested inside
    assert is_nested('[[]][[') == True        # nested pair plus unmatched opens

    # Edge cases
    assert is_nested('') == False             # empty string
    assert is_nested('[[[') == False          # only opening brackets
    assert is_nested(']]]') == False          # only closing brackets
    assert is_nested('[[]') == False          # unmatched opening bracket
    assert is_nested('[]]') == False          # extra closing bracket
    assert is_nested('[') == False            # single open
    assert is_nested(']') == False            # single close

    # Deeper nesting
    assert is_nested('[[[]]]') == True        # triple nesting
    assert is_nested('[][[[]]]') == True      # sequential then nested
    assert is_nested('[[[[[]]]]]') == True    # deep nesting
    assert is_nested('[]][[]') == False       # two separate non-nested pairs

test_is_nested()
print("All tests passed!")
